snippet.title: Most Computer Chips Start in Rock From One Small Town
snippet.description:
Most computer chips start in a quartz crucible, and most of that quartz comes from one small town in North Carolina: Spruce Pine. Why a silicon crystal needs ultra-pure quartz, and what stopped after Hurricane Helene in 2024.

New Shorts every day.

SOURCES
- Wikipedia, Spruce Pine Mining District (about 70 to 90 % of the world's high-purity quartz; molten silicon reacts with almost all materials except quartz above 1,400 C; Helene 2024; stockpiled crucibles prevented immediate shortages): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spruce_Pine_Mining_District
- The Quartz Corp, Silicon wafer production (one crucible pulls about 8 ingots in about 400 hours; a 300 mm ingot yields about 2 million chips): https://www.thequartzcorp.com/silicon-wafer-production
- The Quartz Corp, Geology (pegmatites almost free from inclusions): https://www.thequartzcorp.com/geology
- Sibelco, High-purity quartz (two uniquely pure ore bodies at Spruce Pine; crucibles for the Czochralski process): https://www.sibelco.com/materials/high-purity-quartz
The 16 million chips per crucible is a rough calculation from the Quartz Corp figures above (chip sizes vary). The share of supply differs by source (about 70 to 90 %). Figures checked on 5 October 2026.

PHOTO CREDITS (Wikimedia Commons)
Downtown Spruce Pine, used crucible photos, silicon boule and 1956 crystal puller: public domain | Silicon wafer: Peellden, CC BY-SA 3.0 | Silicon crystal: Massimiliano Lincetto, CC BY-SA 4.0 | Pegmatite rock (Ruggles mine, New Hampshire, shown as an example of the rock type): James St. John, CC BY 2.0 | Hurricane Helene damage (Buncombe County, North Carolina): NCDOT Communications, CC BY 2.0

The narration and the diagrams are AI-generated or drawn for this video; the photos are real.

#semiconductors #quartz #chips #SprucePine #supplychain

snippet.title: The First Metal-Type Book Is Not the Gutenberg Bible
snippet.description:
The first book printed with metal type is not the Gutenberg Bible. It is the Jikji, a Korean book from 1377, and its printer's mistakes are the proof.

New Shorts every day.

SOURCES
- BnF (Bibliotheque nationale de France), Jikji, treasure of the world of printing (printed 1377 at Heungdeok Temple, Cheongju; provenance; free on Gallica): https://bnf.fr/en/jikji-treasure-world-printing
- Global Jikji, Movable Metal Type of Goryeo Korea (the postscript: "printed with cast metal type at Heungdeoksa Temple outside Cheongju Magistracy"): https://www.globaljikji.org/en/sub.do?menukey=4103
- Open Culture, The oldest book printed with movable type is not the Gutenberg Bible (September 2026): https://www.openculture.com/2026/09/the-oldest-book-printed-with-movable-type-is-not-the-gutenberg-bible-jikji.html
- Wikipedia, Jikji (the upside-down, omitted and tilted characters scholars cite as evidence of loose metal type): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jikji
- From Jikji to Gutenberg, University of Utah: https://jikji.utah.edu/
The Gutenberg Bible is dated 1450 to 1455 depending on the source, so the gap is 73 to 78 years. Figures checked on 5 October 2026.

PHOTO CREDITS (Wikimedia Commons)
Jikji pages and Jikji cover: public domain | Jikji open book: Zytheme, CC0 | Gutenberg Bible: Joshua Keller, CC BY 2.0 | Early metal type pieces: Ken Eckert, CC BY-SA 4.0 | Tripitaka Koreana woodblock: Steve46814, CC BY-SA 3.0 | Heungdeoksa: Lawinc82, CC BY-SA 3.0 | Cheongju Early Printing Museum: hyolee2, CC BY-SA 3.0

The narration and the diagrams are AI-generated or drawn for this video; the photos are real.

snippet.title: EV Battery Life: Only 2% a Year, and Charging Matters Most
snippet.description:
Electric car batteries lose about 2% of their capacity a year. What wears them faster (fast charging, heat), what cold really costs (range, mostly the heater), and why packs got cheaper (iron phosphate chemistry).

New Shorts every day.

SOURCES
- Geotab, EV Battery Health Study, 13 January 2026 (2.3% a year across 22,700+ vehicles; fast charging above 100 kW up to 3.0% a year against about 1.5%; hot regions about 0.4% a year more): https://www.geotab.com/press-release/ev-battery-health-degradation-fast-charging-study/
- BloombergNEF, Battery Price Survey, December 2025 ($108 per kWh average pack, down 8%; LFP $81 against NMC $128): https://about.bnef.com/insights/clean-transport/lithium-ion-battery-pack-prices-fall-to-108-per-kilowatt-hour-despite-rising-metal-prices-bloombergnef/
- AAA cold-weather range tests, May 2026 (39% less range at 20 F with climate control; as reported by Autoblog): https://www.autoblog.com/news/aaa-finds-ev-range-drops-39-in-cold-weather-and-costs-jump
- Wang et al., Fast charging of lithium-ion batteries at all temperatures, PNAS 2018 (lithium plating in the cold, SEI growth in the heat): https://ecec.me.psu.edu/Pubs/2018_June_PNAS.pdf
Figures checked on 5 October 2026. The 2.3% is an average, not a guarantee; the claim that most of the cold-weather loss is the cabin heater is the reading of AAA's tests in press summaries.

PHOTO CREDITS (Wikimedia Commons, Flickr)
Battery pack: Gereon Meyer, CC BY-SA 4.0 | Nissan Leaf cutaway: Norsk Elbilforening, CC BY 2.0 | Pack cabling: Norio Nakayama, CC BY-SA 2.0 | Charging site: Daniel Lu, CC BY-SA 4.0 | Desert road: Brocken Inaglory, CC BY-SA 3.0 | Charging posts in snow: Guttorm Flatabo, CC BY 2.0 | Winter road: Bert Kaufmann, CC BY 2.0 | Heat pump: Votpuske, CC BY 4.0 | Pack production: Vigor0503, CC BY-SA 4.0 | LFP cells: Yo-Co-Man, CC BY-SA 4.0

The narration and the electrode schematic are AI-generated (the schematic is simplified); the photos are real.

snippet.title: Why Copper Could Limit the AI Race
snippet.description:
One AI server rack can hold over two miles of copper cable, yet AI is only a small slice of the world's copper. Why a new mine takes about 17 years, and why that could limit the AI race.

New Shorts every week.

SOURCES
• S&P Global, copper supply gap study, 8 January 2026 (17 years from discovery to production; a 25% shortfall by 2040 is a forecast): https://press.spglobal.com/2026-01-08-Substantial-Shortfall-in-Copper-Supply-Widens-as-the-Race-for-AI-and-Growing-Defense-Spending-Add-to-Accelerating-Demand,-New-S-P-Global-Study-Finds
• USGS, Mineral Commodity Summaries 2026, Copper: https://pubs.usgs.gov/periodicals/mcs2026/mcs2026-copper.pdf
• IEA, Global Critical Minerals Outlook 2025: https://www.iea.org/reports/global-critical-minerals-outlook-2025/overview-of-outlook-for-key-minerals
• Nvidia GB200 NVL72, about 5,000 copper cables and over 2 miles per rack (Nvidia's figures, as reported by LightCounting): https://www.lightcounting.com/research-note/april-2024-all-eyes-on-nvidia-352
• Copper in electric cars, 83 kg against 23 kg (ICSG 2018, cited in this study): https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0921344920305152
• How porphyry copper deposits form (Nature Reviews Earth & Environment, 2021): https://www.nature.com/articles/s43017-021-00182-8
Figures checked on 5 October 2026.

PHOTO CREDITS (Wikimedia Commons)
Server rack cables: Derrick Coetzee from Berkeley, CA, USA, CC0 · Native copper: Flipin,OG, CC0 · Transformer busbars: Wtshymanski, CC BY-SA 3.0 · Transmission line: Eduardo Sanchez, CC0 · Electric car charging: Julian Herzog (Website), CC BY 4.0 · Copper pipes: Achim Hering, CC BY 3.0 · Chalcopyrite: Didier Descouens, CC BY-SA 3.0 · Chuquicamata mine: Diego Delso, CC BY-SA 4.0 · Bingham Canyon Mine: David Ratledge, CC BY 4.0, and Farragutful, CC BY-SA 4.0

snippet.title: Lithium Isn't Rare, So Why Do Countries Fight Over It?
snippet.description:
Lithium isn't rare, but about 60% of it is refined in one country. How the lightest metal became a pressure point, and the battery that could walk away from it.

New Shorts every week.

SOURCES
• USGS, Mineral Commodity Summaries 2026, Lithium: https://pubs.usgs.gov/periodicals/mcs2026/mcs2026-lithium.pdf
• IEA, Global Critical Minerals Outlook 2025 (China's share of lithium refining): https://www.iea.org/reports/global-critical-minerals-outlook-2025/overview-of-outlook-for-key-minerals
• China's export licenses for high-end batteries, cathodes and graphite anodes (MOFCOM Decision 58, 9 Oct 2025) and their one-year suspension (Decision 70, 7 Nov 2025): https://www.ess-news.com/2025/10/13/china-imposes-new-export-controls-on-lithium-ion-battery-technology/ and https://www.cirs-group.com/en/chemicals/china-temporarily-suspends-export-controls-on-key-raw-materials-including-rare-earths-lithium-batteries-and-diamond
• CATL's sodium-ion batteries (company claims): https://carnewschina.com/2025/12/28/catl-confirms-2026-large-scale-sodium-ion-battery-deployment-in-multiple-sectors/
• Atacama evaporation ponds: sources give about 12 to 24 months; the video uses about 18, from Albemarle's description.
Figures checked on 5 October 2026.

PHOTO CREDITS (Wikimedia Commons)
Lithium in mineral oil: Sea Moon, CC BY 2.0 · Lithium: W. Oelen, CC BY-SA 3.0 · Lithium-ion cells: Sevenethics, CC0 · Salar de Atacama: NASA Earth Observatory and NASA SVS (public domain), ESA (CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO) · Greenbushes mine: Calistemon, CC BY-SA 4.0 · CATL, Arnstadt: Giorno2, CC BY-SA 4.0 · CATL, IAA 2024: Matti Blume, CC BY-SA 4.0 · NYK Themis at the Port of Los Angeles: Downtowngal, CC BY-SA 4.0 · Container cranes: George Robinson, CC BY-SA 2.0 · Sodium-ion cell: Vladimir022009, CC BY-SA 4.0 · Faradion sodium-ion cell, Science Museum: The wub, CC BY-SA 4.0
